record.paper_title: A New Paradigm for Scattering Theory of Linear and Nonlinear Waves: Review and Open Problems
record.original_question: In nonlinear or multichannel scattering, how can one determine the energies or range of localized asymptotic solutions from the matrix corresponding to free-to-free channel scattering? In particular, in systems such as photon scattering from a multi-particle atom, is observing only a free photon in and a free photon out sufficient to determine all asymptotic channels and localized components?

evidence.quote: Problem 1 How can the energies (range) of localized solutions be determined? Is it possible to ascertain this based on the construction of the matrix corresponding to free-to-free channel scattering?

Even if our observations are restricted to cases with a photon in and a photon out, and even if we limit ourselves to the subspace of the continuous spectrum (of the three-body problem), some states will have three free particles out and some only a bound state and a free photon. Is it feasible to determine everything solely by observing the photon?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a quantum mechanical multichannel scattering system (for example, the scattering of a photon from a multi-particle atomic system, modeled as an N-body Schrödinger or Hamiltonian system with both free and bound asymptotic channels). The Hilbert space decomposes, on the continuous spectrum, into asymptotic channels labeled by clusterings of the particles; each channel has its own free asymptotic dynamics and possibly bound (localized) sub-states. The full S-matrix acts on the direct sum of all asymptotic channel spaces, and contains in particular a sub-block S_{ff} describing scattering from the purely free channel (e.g., one free photon in, one free photon out) into itself.

Question: 
(a) Given only the free-to-free scattering sub-matrix S_{ff} (its kernel, analytic structure, and dependence on the energy parameter), determine whether one can reconstruct the set of energies, or at least the energy ranges, at which localized (bound or partially-bound) asymptotic states exist in the other channels. In other words, is the spectrum of localized sub-states of all channels recoverable from S_{ff} alone?
(b) In the specific situation of a photon interacting with a three-body atomic system, where measurements register only an incoming free photon and an outgoing free photon, determine whether the data of this restricted scattering matrix suffices to identify all asymptotic channels (including those with three free outgoing particles and those with a bound subsystem plus a free photon) and the energies of their localized components.

Provide either a constructive procedure for such a reconstruction, or a proof that the free-to-free sub-matrix is in general insufficient to recover this information.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an explicit open problem in a 2024 review of scattering theory of linear and nonlinear waves. No subsequent literature appears to provide a general answer to whether the free-to-free channel S-matrix alone determines the energies of localized asymptotic states in multichannel/N-body scattering. The question appears to remain open.
